svg.title: Loosening a policy while increasing learning: macaque gaze-choice task, illustrative choice states, and schematic neural and learning differences
svg.desc: Panel A, an abbreviated task strip: a screen with central fixation, then a screen with three identical circular targets at the corners of a triangle around the centre and one saccade arrow from the centre to one target, then an outcome stage showing a fluid drop or an empty outcome, labeled reward or no reward. Position labels 1, 2 and 3 are added outside the screen for teaching only. A note reads reward probabilities change independently. A small electrode icon is labeled FEF recording. Panels B and C compare exploitation, left, with exploration, right. Panel B shows illustrative choice strings: exploitation 1 1 1 1 1 1; exploration 1 3 2 2 3 3; states were inferred from choice history. Panel C shows, for each state, a schematic of three choice-predictive patterns between aligned start and saccade markers: in exploitation they separate earlier and more distinctly; in exploration later and less distinctly. Below each sketch, a dashed arrow of equal thickness runs from outcome to next choices, labeled updates choice for exploitation and greater outcome influence for exploration. A footnote reads recording study; qualitative summary.
